sources: Sena 3 (XAmple-refusal path of L-0 only, on a scratch copy)
copies: every run on a fresh CP4-Scratch- copy, deleted afterwards with its backups (FR-037)

l0-coexistence.json.detail: With the read worker holding a non-shared project (lock PID = the read worker's own interpreter), a second process's OpenProject(writeEnabled=True) raises FP_FileLockedError ('This project is in use by another program'). The same open succeeds once the read worker is released. The two opens cannot coexist; FR-027's 'try_word answers during filing' cannot hold on a non-shared project.
l0-coexistence.json.m1_outcome: M-1 interim restriction STAYS (reads refused during filing on non-shared projects; the read worker is released before the writable open, now unconditionally on non-shared). Per T005, stop as needs_human for a maintainer amendment of FR-027.
l0-coexistence.json.filing_on_production_path: completed, persisted: 1 word filed (reapproved 1, deleted 0 against a projected upper bound of 1); the .fwdata changed; a fresh read worker re-reads the parser-evaluated analysis afterwards
l0-coexistence.json.xample_note: The memory-noted save (parse-worker-saves-xample-project) was NOT reproduced on the try_word engine-refusal path: the Sena 3 copy's sha256 and mtime are unchanged after the refused open and the release. Its root cause lies on a path that gets further than the engine gate (the original test_parse_live run).
defects_found_and_fixed_on_the_way: parser_probe: Assembly.LoadFile did not resolve ParserCore's dependencies in a process that had not imported flexicon, so filing's preflight refused parser_core_missing on a healthy install (and the read-spine probe had the same latent failure); fixed with an AssemblyResolve handler over ParserCore's own folder

handlers/parse: the access gate refused the server's OWN read worker's lock as held_by_other; now recognised (worker reports its own pid in 'ready'; a venv launcher's pid is not the lock holder) and released before re-probing

filing worker: flexicon's HeadlessLcmUI.SynchronizeInvoke is None; HCParser's ParserModelChangeListener subscribes to change notifications, so FieldWorks' filer died with NullReferenceException in SendPropChangedNotifications; fixed with a HeadlessLcmUI subclass returning SIL.LCModel.Utils.SingleThreadedSynchronizeInvoke
runner: a filing run that stopped on an error and then saved recorded error=null; the cause is now recorded

files.q2-agent.json: On both designated projects (ActiveParser == HC) the HermitCrab agent (CmAgentTags.kguidAgentHermitCrabParser = 5093d7d7-4f18-4aad-8c86-88389476df15, named 'HCParser') is owned by LangProject.AnalyzingAgentsOC, and the production probe (probe_hc_agent via DefaultParserAgent) reports state=present.
files.q3-staleness.json: No. Over 5 filed words the filing worker's per-word IsUpToDate() check never came back false: 0 mid-run grammar reloads. Filing analyses does not invalidate the HermitCrab grammar; R-05's per-word gate costs one IsUpToDate() call per word and reloads only when the grammar really changes.
files.q4-checker-reprobe.json: Run live: no public grammar-health checker in ParserCore 9.3.11.0 / HermitCrab 3.8.2.0; the gate keeps its own diff (parent SPEC 9.5.3)
files.q5-checksum.json: Yes. Run 2, in a new filing worker process, reports unchanged = 5 of 5 and filed_words = []; the .fwdata is byte-identical before and after run 2. Wordform.Checksum == ParseResult.GetHashCode() holds across processes, so FLEx's own skip works for MCP runs.

run_mode_note: Every file here came from a live run against FieldWorks on a fresh CP4-Scratch- copy (its name is recorded inside each file); nothing here is mocked. S1, S2+S3 and T081 were re-run independently by lex-verification (reviews/lex-verification.md).
